paper_title: Attributing Response to Context A Jensen-Shannon Divergence Driven   Mechanistic Study of Context Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
caption: Computational efficiency comparison between our ARC-JSD and Contextcite (n=256 calls) across all datasets and RAG models. Each bar represents the average seconds per sample for ARC-JSD and Contextcite with different RAG models and datasets.
model_annotation: The chart titled “Computational Efficiency: ARC-JSD vs. Contextcite” illustrates average computational time per sample for two methods (ARC-JSD and Contextcite) evaluated across multiple datasets and RAG models, with six bars shown for each model corresponding to method–dataset combinations. The horizontal axis is labeled “Models” and lists four categorical groups in left-to-right order: Qwen2-1.5B-IT, Qwen2-7B-IT, Gemma2-2B-IT, and Gemma2-9B-IT. The vertical axis is labeled “Seconds/Sample” and uses a linear numeric scale ranging from 0 up to just under 90, with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 20, 40, 60, and 80 seconds. For each model, six side-by-side (grouped) bars appear in the legend order: ARC-JSD–TyDi QA (dark blue), Contextcite–TyDi QA (orange), ARC-JSD–Hotpot QA (medium blue), Contextcite–Hotpot QA (light orange), ARC-JSD–MuSiQue (very light blue), and Contextcite–MuSiQue (very light orange). Approximate bar heights are: for Qwen2-1.5B-IT, ~1.8 s (ARC-JSD–TyDi), ~4.5 s (Contextcite–TyDi), ~5.0 s (ARC-JSD–Hotpot), ~18 s (Contextcite–Hotpot), ~11 s (ARC-JSD–MuSiQue), and ~27 s (Contextcite–MuSiQue); for Qwen2-7B-IT, ~3.2 s, ~8.5 s, ~10 s, ~26.5 s, ~21 s, and ~61 s respectively; for Gemma2-2B-IT, ~2.0 s, ~5.2 s, ~6.0 s, ~18.2 s, ~12.5 s, and ~35.5 s respectively; and for Gemma2-9B-IT, ~5.0 s, ~13 s, ~15.5 s, ~44 s, ~31.5 s, and ~88–89 s respectively. The models are presented as a fixed categorical sequence rather than being visibly sorted by bar magnitude, and no individual bars appear specially highlighted beyond their color coding and the legend.
